definitions.explanation: The act of changing from one set of clothes to another.
A set of clothes prepared for changing into, such as clean clothes brought on a trip or kept at work.

examples.japanese: {着替|きが}えに{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took time to get changed.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}の{前|まえ}にユニフォームに{着替|きが}えをする。
examples.english: I change into my uniform before the game.

examples.japanese: {更衣室|こういしつ}で{着替|きが}えを{済|す}ませてから{会場|かいじょう}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: After finishing changing in the locker room, I headed to the venue.

examples.japanese: {着替|きが}えを{持|も}ってきた。
examples.english: I brought a change of clothes.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}には{着替|きが}えを{二|ふた}セット{用意|ようい}した。
examples.english: I prepared two sets of spare clothes for the trip.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもはすぐ{汚|よご}すので、{着替|きが}えを{多|おお}めに{入|い}れておいたほうがいい。
examples.english: Children get dirty quickly, so it's better to pack extra changes of clothes.

notes:
USAGE:
{着替|きが}え is a noun derived from the verb {着替|きが}える (to change clothes). It can refer either to the act of changing or to the clothes themselves.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {着替|きが}えを{持|も}つ (to bring a change of clothes)
- {着替|きが}えを{済|す}ませる (to finish changing)
- {着替|きが}えを{用意|ようい}する (to prepare spare clothes)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{衣替|ころもが}え refers to the seasonal switch of wardrobes, not daily changing of clothes. {着替|きが}える is the verb form meaning to change clothes.
